correctness.rationale: For the oriented K_mn incidence matrix, zero row/column sums give Z and P_Z(X)=H_m X H_n; four ordered-cell orbits identify the entire S_m x S_n commutant. Averaging any Z- or B-projection over the isometric finite group is still a projection and yields P_Z or P_B, proving universal minimax, not just a candidate. Entrywise l1 column sums give 4(m-1)(n-1)/(mn) and 3-2/m-2/n+2/(mn), and symmetric matrices give l∞. At m=n=2 Hölder equality makes the line projection unique. Else an alternating 2x2 flow times unused column/row sum is a nilpotent rank-one perturbation: small nonzero real t preserves each absolute column sum, providing genuinely distinct optimal projections, also valid over C. Rank-one test matrices plus column/row operator bounds prove l_p tensorization. Independent exact rational checks for all 2<=m,n<=7 corroborated both constants and perturbations; no bounded enumeration is used to prove the arbitrary-norm assertion.
